facts.value: The Bachelor of Arts program in integrated studies was developed for students whose interests lie beyond established departmental emphases and boundaries. Students work one-on-one with faculty mentors to create a personalized, focused and coherent course of study that draws its curriculum from more than one academic department or college.
The program shares with all other liberal arts and sciences programs the goal of developing analytical abilities and communication skills.
All students are required to meet general university admission requirements.

This program is not available to first-year students. There is an additional application for this degree program. Admission consists of completion of 32 credit hours at ASU with a GPA of at least 3.25, and three letters of recommendation from ASU faculty members.

Students who meet these qualifications and who have faculty mentors in their areas of interest are invited to meet with the Office of Student and Academic Programs in The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences to discuss the possibility of being approved to pursue this opportunity.
Any math course that meets the MATH designation.

The professional and vocational opportunities provided by the integrated studies degree depend on the area of concentration and the particular focus of study. Graduates are prepared to enter the workforce and to pursue graduate and professional studies.
